quickSummary: Concentration terms divide cleanly into temperature-independent (mass-based: m, x_B, %w/w, ppm) and temperature-dependent (volume-based: M, N, %v/v, %w/v). Interconversion formulas allow instant conversion between molarity, molality, density, and mole fractions.
summary: Master all 8 concentration terms, temperature variance, dilution, and interconversion derivations.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5. Concentration Expressions & Temperature Classification
conceptBreakdown.title: 5. Concentration Expressions & Temperature Classification

summaryBox.title: Temperature Invariance Rule
summaryBox.takeaway: Mass-based terms (Molality, Mole Fraction, % w/w) are invariant with temperature. Volume-based terms (Molarity, Normality, % v/v) decrease as temperature rises.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
CONCENTRATION EXPRESSIONS
                                       │
     ┌─────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┐
     ▼                                 ▼                                 ▼
TEMPERATURE-DEPENDENT             TEMPERATURE-INDEPENDENT           VOLUMETRIC NORMALITY
(Volume-based; $V \propto T$)     (Mass-based; invariant)           (Equivalent-based)
├── Molarity ($M$, $\text{mol/L}$) ├── Molality ($m$, $\text{mol/kg}$) ├── Normality ($N$, $\text{eq/L}$)
├── Mass/Vol ($\% w/v$)           ├── Mole Fraction ($x_i$)         └── $N = M \times n\text{-factor}$
└── Vol/Vol ($\% v/v$)            └── Mass Fraction ($\% w/w$)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Mass Percentage (% w/w)**: $\frac{w_B}{w_A + w_B} \times 100$ [T-Independent]
• **Mole Fraction ($x_B$)**: $\frac{n_B}{n_A + n_B}$, where $x_A + x_B = 1$ [T-Independent]
• **Molality ($m$)**: $\frac{n_B}{w_A(\text{kg})} = \frac{w_B \times 1000}{M_B \times w_A(\text{g})}$ [T-Independent]
• **Parts Per Million (ppm)**: $\frac{w_B}{w_{\text{total}}} \times 10^6$ [T-Independent if w/w]
• **Molarity ($M$)**: $\frac{n_B}{V_{\text{soln}}(\text{L})} = \frac{w_B \times 1000}{M_B \times V_{\text{soln}}(\text{mL})}$ [T-Dependent: decreases as T rises]
• **Normality ($N$)**: $\frac{\text{Gram Eq of B}}{V_{\text{soln}}(\text{L})} = M \times n\text{-factor}$ [T-Dependent]

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6. Essential Interconversion Derivations
conceptBreakdown.title: 6. Essential Interconversion Derivations
conceptBreakdown.content:
Let $d$ be solution density in g/mL, $M$ be Molarity, $m$ be Molality, $x_B$ be solute mole fraction, $M_A$ be solvent molar mass (18.015 for water), and $M_B$ be solute molar mass:

1. **Molality from Mole Fraction**:
   $$\mathbf{m = \frac{x_B}{x_A} \times \frac{1000}{M_A} = \frac{x_B}{1 - x_B} \times \frac{1000}{M_A}}$$

2. **Mole Fraction from Molality**:
   $$\mathbf{x_B = \frac{m}{m + \frac{1000}{M_A}}}$$

3. **Molality from Molarity and Density**:
   $$\mathbf{m = \frac{1000 \cdot M}{1000 \cdot d - M \cdot M_B}}$$

4. **Molarity from Mass % (% w/w) and Density**:
   $$\mathbf{M = \frac{(\% w/w) \times d \times 10}{M_B}}$$

5. **Dilution & Mixing Laws**:
   • Dilution: $M_1 V_1 = M_2 V_2$ and $N_1 V_1 = N_2 V_2$
   • Non-Reacting Solution Mixing: $M_{\text{mix}} = \frac{\sum M_i V_i}{\sum V_i}$

quickRevision: Molarity decreases with increasing temperature due to volume expansion.
Molality is moles solute per kg of solvent.
